sentences.text: South Australia’s Independent Commissioner Against Corruption issued guidance on conflicts of interest after investigations repeatedly raised the issue.
sentences.support:
Conflicts of interest have also been a persistent feature in numerous other ICAC 
investigations as well as matters referred to agencies for investigation.

sentences.text: The Commissioner explained that a conflict can arise when personal interests intersect with public duties, including where others could reasonably perceive a conflict.
sentences.support:
A public officer has a conflict of interest when a ‘fair and reasonable’ person 
could perceive them as having one.

sentences.text: The Commissioner concluded that identifying, disclosing and managing conflicts is necessary to protect impartial services and public confidence.
sentences.support:
The appropriate identification, disclosure and management of conflicts of interest is a 
duty incumbent on all public officers and public authorities.

sentences.text: The Commissioner urged public authorities to review their conflict controls and regularly remind staff of their obligations.
sentences.support:
Most importantly, public authorities should regularly instruct their staff on their conflict of 
interest obligations.

findings.quote: There is nothing inherently wrong with having a conflict of interest.

The appropriate identification, disclosure and management of conflicts of interest is a 
duty incumbent on all public officers and public authorities.

notes: The foreword summarises the purpose. This is guidance rather than findings about named individuals; advice is not presented as a numbered recommendations list.
